column1: # France, the Grande Mosquée de Paris: its 2026 table as its Mawaqit page carries it, printed for the
# mosque (ruling R44), split in the local archive (ukfr/split-7g/): January to September, its 2026 method
# (the Moonsighting Committee's seasonal Fajr, Isha = sunset + 90), fit; October to December, which the
# page still carries in its earlier method (its October rows are the mosque's October 2025 rows: Fajr about
# 18° tapering, Isha about 16°, Zuhr + 1), held out. Also held out: the mosque's own September 2026 page
# and its October 2025 rows. No imsak is printed: the Fajr is also where the fast begins (F+E).
# On the earlier method's rows (October to December on the page, and October 2025) the Fajr start and Zuhr
# are not checked: the 2026 method's are 7-16 and 4-5 min later by design (it is the method in force), so they
# are never early there and would only measure the two methods' distance. Every other column is, and Isha
# takes the later of the two methods from October (TwilightCurves' GMP rule). Their Fajr is still checked as
# the end of eating (E, ruling R80): a reader of the page stops eating then, and the end is never after it.
